answer: A timber yard stays honest when every identity is underwritten by a distinct insurer who stakes a bond that is burned if the identity cheats. The first fake costs one bond, the tenth ten bonds, and the twentieth twenty, each bond posted by a different insurer risking real capital. Twenty invented agents would owe 210 bonds. Cheating burns all its bonds at once, so one bad identity wipes out its stake. Bulk farming fails because insurers are finite, each underwrites one newcomer per epoch, and no insurer stakes on twenty strangers at once, like a grove sheltering a single plume of smoke.
